newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars on firm turf ahead jobs.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars on firm turf ahead jobs.

text.p: SIMEX interest rate futures finished on the higher end of narrow trading bands on Friday ahead of the release of the eagerly-awaited U.S. employment report for August, due at 1230 GMT.

A trader with a U.S. institution said the market's recent susceptibility to rate hike concerns indicated that Eurodollar futures could be quickly sold off if the employment data were on the high side of expectations.
Analysts in a Reuters poll expect non-farm payrolls to rise by 224,000 on average in August, compared with July's 193,000 increase.
But a dealer with a British futures house said the market was unlikely to be spooked unless payrolls showed an increase of 300,000 and average hourly earnings were up by 0.3-0.4 percent.
December Eurodollars finished unchanged against their IMM settlement at 93.85. Volume was a low 9,430 lots.
Euroyen futures made a slight recovery on the decline in Tokyo stocks, with the most active March contract ending at 99.06 against its CME close at 99.05. Its low was 99.03.

Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita's statement that Japan's economic recovery was not yet self-sustainable also gave credence to the growing perception Japan would not follow the United States in raising rates.
"It's almost a hundred percent clear that the BOJ won't do anything this side of Christmas no matter what the Fed does," said the trader with the European institution.

Japanese government bond futures for December received a boost from large-lot buying of the September contract by players holding long positions ahead of the contract's expiry on Friday. December JGBs settled at 120.64 against their opening 120.56.
